As we all know The Tekken series has a long-standing reputation in arcades. Tekken 7 is an incredibly tense game of jabs, feints, and sidesteps because any hit may lead to a long combo sting. Factor in characters with move sets that emulate real martial arts, interactive stages that let you knock people through floors and walls, and terrific slowdown effects that happen when both fighter's health bars are red and they perform close quarter melee attacks and you have a fighting game that's essentially an interactive martial arts flick. Tekken 7 is a fantastic game and one of the best entries in the series.

+ Tekken finally has a PC-port and it's fantastic! 

The entire version is objectively the best with fantastic graphics, short load-times and tons of peripheral support. This is a perfect example of a series transitioning to PC! If you like fighting-games, this is an absolute must-buy!

+Fantastic mechanics that are fun for all

Tekken has a low barrier to entry, but a massive skill-ceiling. You can buy this game and have a fantastic time even if you have never played a fighting game before. For the serious player the game features insane depth and a lot to enjoy. Tekken 7 has changed things such as throw-breaking and made things generally more streamlined, but maintained it's complexety and depth. This really is the best Tekken has ever been. 

+Optimized roster

While not perfect, the roster is tightened up. Your favorite is most likely still in the game and the newcomers are generally good. Each character feels unique and I feel Namco has made good decisions on which characters to keep.

+Hype as fuck final boss

Just play the story and see for yourself.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-Lack of content in general

I would like to underline that this game has already been out for 2 years in arcades. While not the FR-version, the game has techinally been complete. This begs the question of what in the fuck Namco has been doing for 2 years. Customization is a joke compared to Tekken 6 and there are very few modes. There is also no replay-mode or anything outside the basic ranked online.

The story-mode is very short and the scenarios for other characters are just abysmal. These scenarios are basically a random fight with an in-engine cutcene that does the bare minimum of fan-service. Every Tekken-game before this has had far more fleshed out content story-wise in general. Also, the customization is especially sadening considering that there are so few characters and one would assume this means more options for each one. 

-Mediocre story-mode

The story-mode is short and nothing to really brag about. It has some cool moments (and Akuma), but it's basically a bunch of CG-cutcenes tied together with a terrible narrator and a hamfisted plot. The story makes no sense, but I can't really fault the game for it. Tekken has always been bonkers. However, compared to many other fighters it really falls flat and it has to be pointed out considering that the game offers very little other content.

-No tutorials or help for newcomers

The game has absolutely no tutorial and it's honestly baffling. Tekken is not an easy game to get into. Sure you can mash buttons as Eddy, but there is only a question of time until someone bodies you. It's easy to feel lost in this game, yet the game makes very little effort to teach you anything. You are going to end up on YouTube and other sites to figure out combos, frame-data etc. and that isn't good. There should at least be something here to teach new players the basics.

-Online has flaws

As of writing this there are several big problems with online that will hopefully be fixed soon. First of all, rage-quitting is a SERIOUS problem. There is basically no punishment for quitting and if a player disconnects on you, you don't get the win. This becomes an even bigger problem in Tekkens tournament-mode. If the host gets mad he can kick you immediately or outright leave to shut down the entire lobby. As a result, playing Tournament-mode is rather difficult.

Connecting to other players is also very difficult as of right now. Connecting through the match-list is almost hopeless and filled with error messages. The best option is using warm-up and wait for a match to be suggested by the matchmaking system. However, this is also frustratingly difficult. It can take 3-4 requests before you can accept a request to fight that actually works. As a result you will often end up in games with 3-bar connections because the game has not been able to connect to the players that fit the criteria you searched for. Most of the time you will be told that "the connection to the opponent has been lost". You might think that this is your potential opponent declining your request, but in the majority of times it is in fact the game struggling to connect. However, this will most likely be fixed and when it happens I will remove this from the review.

If you want to buy this game, I have a few tips: 

First, watch AvoidingthePuddle on YouTube. He has a playlist of videos where he goes over the fundamentals of the game in probably the most entertaining manner possible. Generally just keep up with this guy if you want to follow the game.

Second, get into the competitive scene. Fighting games are a lot more fun when you're playing them with other people, and doing things like going to local tournaments can help you learn the game even better. Watching professionals play the game is also pretty fun and educational as well.

Third, pick a character and go with it. Tekken, at most skill levels, is probably one of the most balanced fighting games out there, and don't let stoners convince you otherwise. DLC characters are fun to play with but cost a bit of money, so maybe explore a bit of that character before buying anything.

Finally, stay calm and be respectful. There are plenty of people in this community who will be rude inside the game and out. Keep your cool or else the game doesn't become fun. Also, make it a point to NOT message Harada or Michael Murray on Twitter.

If you stick with it, Tekken can be a very fun and rewarding experience. There's so many intricacies to it that allow you learn something about it every time you play it. There are more people following this game now than ever, so now is the time to jump into it.

[b]The first game I ever Pre-Ordered, and It was worth It!, Tekken has been a legendary franchise in the world of fighting games, dominating arcades, PlayStation consoles, and tournaments for decades. But for years, PC players could only dream of experiencing Tekken on their platform. There were always rumors floating around that Tekken would finally come to PC, but nothing ever materialized, until Tekken 7 finally dropped on Steam.

I still remember the excitement and disbelief when the official announcement came. Without a second thought, I pre-ordered Tekken 7 immediately—the first pre-order of my life! And let me tell you… it was worth every penny.[/b]

[h1]The Ultimate Fighting Experience[/h1]
[b]Tekken 7 stays true to its roots while bringing new mechanics, characters, and an exciting cinematic story mode. It’s the most polished and visually stunning Tekken game ever made, and playing it on PC at higher resolutions and frame rates makes the experience even better.

Whether you’re a casual player, a hardcore competitor, or just here for the insane story and epic fights, Tekken 7 delivers in every way possible.[/b]

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Tekken is Finally on PC!: After years of waiting, PC players can finally experience the best of Tekken, with smooth performance, high FPS, and crisp visuals.
[*]Beautiful Graphics & Smooth Gameplay: Powered by Unreal Engine 4, Tekken 7 looks absolutely gorgeous, with detailed character models, fluid animations, and jaw-dropping stages.
[*]Incredible Combat System: Tekken’s deep combat mechanics are intact, with a huge roster, responsive controls, and intense fights that reward skill and practice.
[*]New Rage System: The introduction of Rage Arts and Rage Drives adds cinematic and strategic depth, making comebacks even more hype.
[*]A Cinematic Story Mode: The Mishima Saga gives us a dramatic conclusion to the legendary Heihachi vs. Kazuya rivalry.
[*]Amazing Controller Support: Whether you play on keyboard, controller, or arcade stick, the controls feel flawless.
[*]Awesome Roster with DLC Expansions: A mix of classic favorites and new fighters, plus guest characters like Negan from The Walking Dead, Noctis from Final Fantasy XV, and Akuma from Street Fighter!
[/list]
[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Weak Base Content at Launch: When the game first dropped, it lacked fan-favorite modes like Survival, Team Battle, and Customizable Practice Mode (some of which were added later).
[*]DLC Overload: While the DLC characters are amazing, it feels like too many classic fighters were locked behind paid DLC.
[*]No True Tekken Force Mode: Many players were hoping for a proper Tekken Force or Beat ‘Em Up mode, but it never happened.
[*]Online Play Can Be Inconsistent: While netcode improvements have been made, the online experience can still be hit-or-miss, especially against faraway opponents.
[/list]
[h1]Conclusion: A Dream Come True for Tekken Fans[/h1]
[b]Tekken 7 coming to PC was something that felt impossible for so long, and when it finally happened, it was an emotional moment for every longtime fan. The game delivers everything great about Tekken while introducing new mechanics and stunning visuals.

If you love fighting games, this is an absolute must-buy. If you’ve never played Tekken before, this is the perfect entry point to start mastering one of the deepest and most satisfying fighting games ever made.

10/10 – Buy it. Play it. Love it.
(Crying while writing this because Tekken is finally on PC!)[/b]

Tekken 7 is an excellent game with character designs, gameplay, and overall depth. A legendary series and its quality is still unmatched in 3D fighters. The game offers a wide range of characters to choose from. Each character has a distinct feel and playstyle. The roster has hundreds of moves and is capable of rich player expression. There are great in-game learning tools (replay system/punishment training) and plenty of guides to watch online. Other than these positives, there are significant drawbacks to consider.

-The Netcode of this game is not the best. Connection issues are common. You will be dealing with lag at times. 

-Also, please consider some people love to "plug" (disconnect) whenever they lose a heated battle. So they don't lose points while losing credibility. (The game scores a player's disconnect rate. You can see it before you get into a match with them.) Double-checking before accepting players who have a high disconnect rate should do it. (Anything above %2.0 if you ask me.)

-You'll feel hopeless at times. After facing smurfs / literal cheaters (auto block/auto punish etc.) and lag cheaters (lag created by the opponent whenever you attack or have to defend a throw). 

-Although in quick and ranked matches, players won't see their opponent's name until both parties accept the matchup. There are three indicators to distinguish players from one another before getting into the match. The indicators are Region / Language / Disconnection Rate. These could help you to avoid certain matchups or players in your play session. Said regions have six colors (red, blue, yellow, purple, pink, and grey).

-Until you learn how to deal with them, characters with gimmicky moves, mashers, and spammers will test your mental endurance.

Even if you survive this unpleasant environment and keep playing (especially) ranked mode, I have one last thing to share.

-After hitting "Ruler Ranks" (17th / 20th rank) you will most likely be facing top-ranked (29th / 30th rank) players who want to rank up their side characters. The first reason is they play the game more than other players do. The second reason is when you hit the highest rank, every other character you haven't played will jump to ruler ranks automatically. This scaling works on lower-ranked players as well.

Hopefully, Tekken 8 will resolve most of these issues. 

Still, Tekken 7 can be an incredible experience if you match up with people who have some dignity or whenever you play with your friends for fun <3

Every once in a while I feel I find a game that is the epitome of its genre. Tekken is a fighting game in its purest form. If you are looking for a game to obsess over, Tekken can keep your attention for the rest of time. If you are feeling extremely competitive then this game will scratch that itch. Every character has a VASTLY different playstyle and each comes with their own sort of reputation. Nina and Kazuya players know how to get real serious. Yoshimitsu and Panda players know how to party. Law and Dragunov can explode at any moment and they'll keep you on the edge of your seat. King and Devil Jin players are ready to make a spectacle. There are so many martial arts styles covered like Capoeira, Sambo, Majiquan, Boxing, and recently Muay Thai and Wing Chun. 

A couple of warnings. The balance can sometimes be a little off. DLC characters sometimes come out a lot stronger than other characters and there's not much a player can do about that except try their best. Back in Season 2 they accidentally made Akuma (Yes, the guy from Street Fighter) a little too powerful and a couple people started pulling off 100% combos in tournament. More recently Season 3 buffed almost every character and there was a big power creep. Leroy Smith was released and was so good that they had to make a new spot on the teir list. The online can be pretty bad at times and there's not a lot that can be done about it at this point. Unreal Engine is fantastic but it has limitations like anything else. I haven't played much single player and from what I've seen it's not why you buy this game. You unlock every cosmetic (Except DLC) after 2,000 fights so don't grind for unlocks. 

That said this game is wonderful. When you do get locked into a good game with someone, Tekken gets very immersive! It's like playing lightning chess. Both players are making plans on the fly. You are both thinking about high/mid/low/grab/rage/(!) mixups, frame advantage, spacing/side stepping, the stage, character movesets, mental conditioning, recognizing habits, and just trying to outwit the other player. It's not over until the announcer says KO, you can come back and win even if you only have 1 HP left. The depth of this game is astounding. No other fighting game can keep your attention like Tekken. There's a huge amount of player freedom: characters often have multiple taunts, secret moves, silly moves like backflips and  that can do damage, so many fun stances,  This game has a steep learning curve that never really levels off. There is always more to learn and you can always get better. There will always be a new challenge to overcome. 

I play mostly online but there is a thriving global tournament scene. It's a mix of old arcade players and younger fighting game rookies. There are still new players all the time so don't worry about not finding someone that matches your abilities. You can always find someone in a Discord server ready to play. 

If you ever see me online just know that I'm always trying to clown around. I'll throw you over my shoulder into the wall to finish the round because I'm winning and I'm having fun.

Edit: Season 4 is a huge improvement. They rebalanced some aspects of the game and it got rid of the unreasonable combo damage some characters were getting. Also the netplay got an update, and while some matches are still a stuttery mess, most feel like flawless rollback netcode with just a very slight manageable delay. 

The future of the series is uncertain, but I can say this is probably the best that Tekken has ever been. There are new players all the time so don't be afraid to jump in and start from scratch. This is by far the best fighting game I have ever played.
In retrospect: This game was great and I didn't appreciate it enough. Now I miss it dearly.

I previously only had casual/limited experience playing fighting games but in July 2019 I bought Tekken 7 for PlayStation 4 on a whim and can honestly say that the decision to do so completely changed my life. I subsequently bought both the Xbox One and PC versions of the game just so I could play against as many different people as possible. I've put in well over 1,800 hours of gameplay across all three versions (1,350 of which are on Xbox) and have gone from being a total noob to reaching the online rank of True Tekken God (rank 35) with my main (Kuma) -- there are 37 ranks in Tekken 7, each one exponentially more difficult to achieve than the last as you must defeat opponents within two ranks of yourself to rank up, but losses to opponents within two ranks of yourself will cause you to rank down. Never before have I spent so much time outside of a game looking to improve my skills by reading strategies online and watching videos of professionals in an effort to become ranked as highly as I possibly can.

Tekken 7 gives back as much as you put in and even over 22,000 matches later there are still numerous techniques I'm yet to master and moves I'm yet to commit to memory with the character I main -- consider the fact that there are 50 characters on the roster and you have one hell of a deep fighting game. There is never a moment wasted whilst playing as you're always learning something new and honing your skills. The way the momentum can instantly shift due to a perfectly-timed counter hit or whiff punish makes each match so dynamic and exhilarating, and it means that epic comebacks are never out of the question.

However, that's not to suggest that the game is perfect. The load times are very lengthy (made more frustrating by the inability to instant rematch), the netcode is poor, the user interface is dull, the visuals are dated, there are very few modes, there is no proper tutorial, and rage quitters are common as there is minimal punishment for doing so. So, to put it another way, the game has clear flaws but none of them relate to the actual core gameplay which is truly sublime and as close to perfection as I've ever come across in a video game. 

Tekken 7 is an absolute masterpiece and has become, without question, my favourite competitive multiplayer game of all time. I'm 33 years old and have been a hardcore gamer all my life but no other game has even come close to the enjoyment, adrenaline, satisfaction, and sense of achievement that winning a single close-fought round in Tekken 7 can give me. If you're considering this game for its single-player then there are certainly better options out there, but when it comes to multiplayer fighting games then Tekken 7 simply has no equal.

If you like competetive fighting games, it's a must buy. If you don't, watch some Tekken 7 tournaments first, it might convert you.

Playing Tekken 7 feels like opening an old photo album you didn’t know you still cared about.
When I was a kid, Tekken 3 was one of the earliest games that pulled me into gaming. Back then it wasn’t about frame data, ranked matches, or competitive play. It was just a kid sitting in front of a screen, pressing random buttons, watching characters kick each other across the arena, and thinking it was the coolest thing in the world. Those afternoons felt endless.
Years later, launching Tekken 7 hits differently. The graphics are sharper, the mechanics are deeper, and the fights are far more intense. But underneath all the polish and chaos, it still carries the same soul that made the series special in the first place.
Seeing familiar characters again almost feels like running into old friends you haven’t seen in years. The Mishima family drama is still as ridiculous as ever, yet somehow that absurdity is part of the charm. The combat is fast, satisfying, and surprisingly technical once you start learning the system. At the same time, you can still mash buttons and enjoy the spectacle just like a kid discovering the series for the first time.
What makes Tekken 7 special isn’t just that it’s a great fighting game. It’s that it quietly reconnects you to where your gaming journey began.
Some games entertain you for a few hours.
Others remind you why you started playing games at all.
Tekken 7 does both.

Tekken 7 is a great game, but in a bad shape. To make this review look neat, I have organized it into bullet points.


**Story: The Mishima Saga & Character Episodes**

Good: 
  - The story has some cool fight scenes.
  - In many fighting games, the way the characters start a fight feels awkwardly forced. In Tekken 7, it has an interesting 
    and a unique way to start a fight. My favourite ones are when Akuma VS Kazuya on the G.Corp Helipad stage (Day) and 
    Heihachi VS Kazuya in the Brimstone and Fire stage.
  - Story CPU characters and enemies can be quite challenging if you try the story on the hardest difficulty. Shin Akuma on 
    the other hand...
  - The has some emotion because you can actually feel some sympathy when Heihachi he killed Kazumi. This is a good 
    thing because Tekken 6's story mode (Scenario Campaign) lacked by a lot.
  - It is neatly organized into chapters with interesting titles.
  - Some of the character episodes in this game are good, the rest...
  - Best part; You get to relive the intro from Tekken 5 and can actually play the destroyed Honmaru temple while fighting 
    the JACK-4 squad (Which also explains why JACK-4 was not a playable character in Tekken 4).

Bad:
  - The story was short, more could have been done.
  - The narrator made the story so boring, I couldn't last a second by listening to the narrator. Imagine someone in real says 
    this to you, in such a monotone and robotic voice, "My home got burnt to the ground and family died in the war".
  - Most of the character episodes are short and terrible.
  - Shin Akuma is annoying to fight against.
  - Some of the characters like Jin and Lars had less screen time because it was all focused on Heihachi and Kazuya.
  - Kazuya, my favourite character, had terrible writing.
  - The DLC characters, except Eliza, do not have an ending.


**Online**

Good:
  - The first Tekken game to have a rematch option.
  - The first Tekken game to have an online tournament mode.
  - The first Tekken game to have a rank points system (added in season 2).
  - We have suffered in past for not having rematch option and rank points system, so it is a blessing to have these features.
  - Tekken Prowess (added in season 4) encourages you to try other characters to increase your prowess.
  - Internet Indication (added in season 4) can allow players to see if their opponents are using an Ethernet cable or or WiFI.
  - The camera system has a unique way of allowing players to play on one side. For example, if both players are playing on 
    the same side, the camera system will adjust both of your screens for enhanced playability.
  - On the online VS screen, you can see the player's stats like Rage Usage, Combo Damage, Aggressiveness, etc.
  - The colour of your name changes, depending on your Tekken Prowess.

Bad:
  - The netcode is bad.
  - When an opponent disconnects on the online vs screen, that opponent will jump straight to the menu while you're stuck 
    on the vs screen for an eternity.
  - No actual consequences for disconnecting. Giving a penalty is nothing. At least Street Fighter V is doing something 
    about this.
  - No dedicated servers, considering that this game was made on a small budget. This is all due to the commercial failure 
    of Tekken Tag Tournament 2.
  - For some reason, your online rank, not being saved in an online sever, but on your hard drive where it contains files that 
    requires no encryption. What this means is that if you get demoted online, you can backup your rank by copy-pasting 
    your old save file into a new one and you'll get your rank back like nothing, as if your previous losses never happened. 
    We call this "safe-scumming".
  - When an opponent disconnects during a match, in an online tournament, either you win by default, or the whole 
    tournament gets disbanded.
  - Online is filled with hackers, cheaters and boosters.
  - Online leaderboards are definitely contaminated with boosters and fake ranks.
  - The online waiting room has no options for practice like in offline practice mode and you cannot pick a stage of 
    your own choice. Instead, you will be playing in an infinite stage (similar to the online waiting room in Tekken Tag 
    Tournament 2) and the music the same from the Geometric Plane stage.
  - The host of an online player session room should have the ability to choose which opponent to fight.
  - For some reason, you cannot back out of the character select screen in online after picking a side. All you can do is pick 
    a character, exit out of online training and will be directed back to the online menu mode.


**Offline**

Good:
  - Practice mode has a lot of options like punishment training (added in season 3).
  - Playing Treasure Battle allows you to unlock items.
  - Inputs can be shown for Rage Art and Rage Drive on the offline versus screen.

Bad:
  - Arcade mod is lacklustre. It only has five stages to complete.
  - The AI is weak, which makes Arcade and Treasure Battle boring.
  - Missing game modes like Survival and Team Battle.
  - General lack of offline modes.


**My Replay and Tips**

Good:
  - You can see replays of your previous battles and learn from your losses.
  - Has a lot of options like input display, frame data, attack info, etc., while watching your replay.
  - Replays can be saved.

Bad:
  - It was added in season 3. We had to wait for a very long time for this feature to be added.
  - Regular replays and saved replays get deleted after an update.


**Customization**

Good:
  - Ability to customize the border of the healthbar.
  - Character panels can be customized further and can be seen on the online VS screen.

Bad:
 - Poor character customization.
 - Most of the characters panels are awful.
 - Lacks a lot of options like decals from Tekken Tag Tournament 2 and many options of clothing from Tekken 6. Thankfully, 
   we have mods for that.
 - Healthbar customization should have had more options.


**Gallery**

Good:
  - Contains artwork and short music video clips (PACHI Slot) you have likely never seen before.
  - You get to watch character endings and look at artwork from previous Tekken titles.

Bad:
  - No option for pausing, going backwards or fast-forwarding when watching the cutscenes If you exit out of a curscene by 
    mistake, you will be taken back to the beginning. Just watch the endings on YouTube.


**ULTIMATE TEKKEN BOWL**

Good:
  - Relive the memories of playing Tekken Bowl from Tekken Tag Tournament.
  - A lot of fun.

Bad:
  - This mode should have been made for online as well.


**General**

Good:
  - The music is amazing
  - The new combo extender, referred to as 'screw' or 'tailspin', makes the combos more fun than 'bound' from Tekken 6. 
    Bound from Tekken 6 still exists, but the new combo extender makes your combos look better.
  - The graphics look amazing.
  - The first Tekken to be on PC.
  - The first Tekken to have controller setup on the character select screen.
  - Controller setup is way better and easy than in previous Tekken titles.
  - Unique character intros occur when you pick specific characters (e.g, Kazuya VS Kazumi or Akuma VS Jin/Devil Jin).
  - The first Tekken to have guest characters like Geese Howard from Fatal Fury/King of Fighters, Noctis Lucis Caelum from 
    Final Fantasy and Negan from the TV series; The Walking Dead.
  - Akuma and Geese look better in Tekken 7 than in their original games.
  - The first Tekken to have frame data display.

Bad:
  - No tutorial
  - Fight money can be used to unlock customization items and content from the gallery. But once you unlock everything, 
    the fight money is completely useless.
  - If you do not want to use fight money, you can still unlock everything by playing nearly 2,000 matches in total.
  - OG characters are locked behind a paywall.
  - Frame Data was added in season 3 and you have to pay for it.
  - Akuma and the rest of the DLC characters are broken.

[i]“Worth the Wait”[/i]
says one of the plates you can customize your online appearance with and it sums up Tekken’s first release on PC very nicely. After more than 20 years PC gamers receive one of the most complex and in depth fighting game experiences. It’s a treat that was long overdue.
 
[i]Played by many, mastered by few.[/i]
As a fighting game, Tekken 7 excels in everything you’d expect from a 3d fighter. Movement in any possible direction. Combos and Blocking are only half of this games very in depth concepts and mechanics. Sidestepping, ducking, back dashing out of an opponents attacks to punish them hard was never this fun and is a key for survival. New players might be a bit overwhelmed by the complexity Tekken 7 comes with, while veterans will feel at home here.
 
[b]Tekken 7 comes with:[/b]
- 38 characters with different fighting & playstyles to choose from
- short, but engaging, fun and easy to follow Story Mode
- leveling up ranks separated from Online & Offline Modes
- Online Mode: Ranked, Player Matches, Lobby & up to 8 Player Tournament Mode
- Offline Mode: Arcade, Treasure Battle, Practice Mode
- Arcade Mode lets players experience the arcade version of Tekken 7
- Treasure Battle rewards players with Fight Money, Customization Items & Special Battles
- Practice Mode is very detailed and allows to learn movesets or to recreate any possible match situation players faced in online matches
- customize characters looks with different clothes, hairstyles, gimmicks etc.
- customize your online appearance by changing health bars, plates & titles
- Gallery Mode: Every existing cutscene & artwork from all previous Tekken games
 
[b]Story Mode[/b]
The long lasting vendetta of father and son that pulled the world into chaos will reach its end in the short but engaging Story Mode. One of them will survive while the other will perish. You will follow some of the series fabled characters along their way until the surprising climax.
Characters not part of the main story receive additional stories in which long overdue loose story ends find closure while others end in hilarious but for the the series usual joke endings.
Story Mode also includes various diffiulties including a baby mode that lets players execute full combos by the push of a single button. It's a nice idea but can't replace real training or a fully fledged Tutorial Mode, which this game is lacking. Many brand new players will have a hard time online when they find out that they have to execute long combo strings all by themselves.

[b]Practice Mode[/b]
But there is Practice Mode featuring endless possibilities of training. New players can practice in this very detailed mode that let's them recreate all imaginable matchup situations they may stumble upon while fighting online. They can easily learn every characters movelist by watching examples or button prompts on screen. Blocking can also be trained by setting the CPU controlled sparing partner to repeat up to 5 moves from their movelist. How to punish, when to side- or backstep? All fundamentals can be learned trough self imposed training. 

[b]Offline Mode[/b]
Besides Arcade and Versus Mode, Treasure Battle is the only other offline feature the game got. Treasure Battle combines the survival and ghost battle of previous games into one. Players can increase their characters offline rank by fighting an endless amount of CPU controlled opponents while unlocking customization items and earning fight money. Opponents also increase in rank and get harder to beat the higher the player climbs the ranked ladder. By keeping a winning streak special battles will appear that net winners even better loot. It's a very entertaining, ongoing challenging mode that should together with practice mode prepare newcomers for online play.

[b]Online Mode[/b]
After beating the Story Mode, climbing the offline rank ladder and spending hours of self imposed training, players can go online to face real life opponents. Before playing rank I suggest matching against players in normal Online Battles or join others in lobbies for up to 6 players to test their skills with one another. I will be real with you guys. Tekken is an extremely technical and complex game. The higher your rank, the better your opponents. Only the most dedicated beginners will survive on higher ranks.

[b]Soundtrack[/b]
I personally love the soundtrack and even listen to it outside the game. The music is a heavily electronic centered mix of IDM, Drum & Bass and Dubstep. It’s modern and may be not to everyones liking. But it’s loud, energetic and keeps you awake from start to finish. Exactly how a soundtrack for a fast paced fighting game should be.
 
[b]Conclusion[/b]
There is not many shortcomings to complain about. Featuring a complex and balanced in depth fighting system dedicated newcomers as well as veterans can enjoy, even though it lacks a proper tutorial mode to explain its mechanics. Self imposed training is a must! Customization is nice, but could be a little bit more refined. After 20 years, Tekken is finally available on PC! So what are you waiting for? Get it!

In this seventh part the conclusion of the Mishima saga is told. The story is told through a reporter and you also play the story mode with characters that the story is being told about.
It all starts quietly through some kind of introduction where it started.
Little Kazuya is pissed because Heihachi killed his mother.

When you are done with the story mode there is another mode where you can perform a player story battle.
These are short fights of 2 rounds against a rival from the series. Jin vs Hwoarang for example.
For example, these fights have a short intro with a small cut scene and you no longer have to defeat 10 or 20 enemies to see the story per character.

Tekken 7 tries to make up for its lack of a superlative single player with sophistication and nostalgia.
For example, the game lets you create playlists with the music from all previous Tekken games, for example.
And the Gallery is the biggest nostalgia bomb since a Smash Bros. game; for example, I really enjoyed watching all Tekken 3 ending movies a little too much.

Another smaller addition to the combat system is the Power Crush.
These are normal attacks, but with one big advantage: they are not interrupted by high and mid attacks.
So the only way to stop a Power Crush is to perform a low attack or a roll.
Among other things, it made me stay a little closer to my opponent than usual, so that I could immediately perform a low kick or throw if I saw him or her perform a Power Crush animation.

1. After purchasing the frame data add on, go to training and skim through the characters to get an idea of what fighting style you like to play with. 

2. After you pick a character, go into the training mode and learn what counter combos your character uses and what frames they are. You can also practice with a CPU in training and itll tell you what counter should be used against what move. 

3. you can go into Treasure battle to unlock more outfits for your character (i believe thats the only way to unlock outfits). Or you can go straight into online mode. 

4. dont be discouraged when playing online, there are some smurfs out there (just like most games); however, view it as a learning opportunity to go through your replays and see what moves they used frequently and then go to training and learn the counter plays to them. 

5. There are mods to help customize your character that you'll be able to find and they are well worth it (only youll be able to see your mod, not other players). 

6. Most importantly HAVE FUN

You've no doubt gotten reviews from professional Tekken 7 players that have put in thousands of hours. Those testimonies are a mixture of both unrequited love and seething hatred. Tekken 7 has been a different game at different stages in its' development just as we are different people at various points in our lives! Anyway,here's a review from a total scrub whom likes fighters but doesn't pursue them as an e-sport career choice!

I'll level, I'm not a fan of the current business model when it comes to fighting games. You put down money for the core foundation and then season passes get released adding characters,modes,and outfits. In my day there was no way for a game to receive internet updates so it came to us in a much more complete state. "Extra content" was unlocked
merely by meeting certain requirements whilst playing. While certain fighters did have those annoying "super turbo alpha editions" releases a few months to a year later the price was quickly reduced because the devs and corpos knew they had to throw us a complimentary bone for buying the previous iterations. It was still a bit shady and a bit anti-consumer but compared to how things are now I wish we could jump into a time-machine and travel back to the friggin 90's!

Having gotten that off my chest,Bandai Namco make great fighting games. At the very least if you can weather the storm and wait until the penultimate definitive version drops then goes on sale you are in for a very good time. I did that previously with Soul Calibur 6 and it is one of the rare gems that stayed on my pc consistently after I downloaded it. I've put around 33+ hours into that tale of souls and swords without being a super competitive "FGC" champion.

Tekken 7 Definitive edition will offer you the following.....

+An enormous  roster. Many old favorites and many brand new faces. You will not be left wanting when it comes to variety.

+A beautiful presentation. Characters look great,backgrounds look great,"everything" looks great. 

+ The fighting game mechanics are easy to understand. You do not have to feel intimidated. The tutorials and even the story mode lay it all out in simple terms. However, though Tekken is noob friendly it is still a momentous task to master. Be aware of that before choosing a higher difficulty or going online.

+Guest characters play just like they do in their respective franchises. I was pleasantly surprised by that after taking Akuma for a spin. 

+By the way, I thought the plot and narrative were presented better than certain people give them credit for. If you like cyberpunk,mysterious shadowy organizations,scary Japanese folk-lore,supernatural shenanigans,messed up family dramas,and epic biblical revelations tier end-of-the world scenarios Tekken 7 certainly goes hard...

+Treasure mode is my jam. Earning in game gold to unlock a wealth of extra content has always appealed to my inner dragon. (Get it? Dragons like hoards of plundered riches!)

+Most of the men are masculine. Most of the women are feminine. There's also diverse representation without sycophantic pointless pandering. Sexy and cool looking outfits can be unlocked for both genders. And you know what? No normal people in any demographic have a beef with this. (Perfectly balanced as all things should be!) 

+There are certain sequences in story mode where you can mow down incoming baddies with actual guns. No joke! (America,frick yeah!)

+Narcoleptic sleepy goth vampire girl ended up being more endearing than I thought she would be!

+You have your throws,reversals,high jabs,low jabs,high kicks,low kicks,mid attacks,juggles,pins,side-steps,holds,grapples,and near-death desperation specials.  Despite Tekken being equal parts "SCP",robot-wars,horror themed family soap opera,bear-brawling,and monster-mash the moment to moment fisticuffs are grounded in realistic martial arts fundamentals. (Er,mostly!)

+One of the better Tekken soundtracks to date. Props to the composers! 

Gripes

-Julia Chang has become a youtuber. (Like and subscribe!) Why? Wasn't she originally a humble ecologist outdoors tom-boy type?

-Kazumi is gonna knock you out! Kazumi gonna scream and shout! Kazumi gonna let her tiger roam about!
 
-"Bro,that's not my final devil form! "This" is! Peeeeeeeeeeeew!"

-Tekken bowling? (Suppresses Iori-like maniacal laughter) Alright I'll level,it's "kinda" fun! But y'know,we could have gotten a refined "beat em up mode" similar to the one in Tekken 6 with more polish! Yeah,that would have been swell.

-No tag-team mode. I realize this isn't a Tekken-Tag entry but it would have been so easy to include. I briefly played the tag-mode in DOA 5 and it was a delight. Shame something similar is missing here.

-Story mode despite its' high production values is "short". Enjoyable but short. Additionally not every character got a fleshed out prologue/epilogue. I feel as if previous Tekken games handled this better. The Mishima saga stuff has top tier production values and visual spectacle in spades but the ball was dropped elsewhere. I compare all this to an entertaining block-buster movie you see with your friends. Fun was had by all but if you take a moment to  think about it "honestly" the presentation was much better than the overall plot and the character development.

-Certain outfits cost "a lot of money" when in comparison to others without rhyme or reason.

-Negan. Negan?! He fits well enough into Tekken's war-torn world whilst simultaneously sticking out like a sore thumb. Was there that much overlap between fighting fans and Walking Dead fans? You have to admit,Negan is an odd inclusion. I mean we could have had Mai Shiranui,Jun,Jinpachi,Iori Yagami,Cammy White,Chun Li,Terry Bogard,or "anyone else" instead....

(Glad they at least put in Armor-King. I thought he was left out but then realized he made the cut!)

Neutral

+/- "Smurfing" in the competitive online circuit. That's when someone logs out at the cusp of defeat so they don't drop in their ranking. To some folks that is going to be infuriating.

However, if you enjoy fighters non-competitively and would not be caught dead at an EVO event even if someone paid you then it's not an issue.

To me "rank and trophies" only mean something if you train at the gym and win in a "real" martial arts tournament. That takes dedication and skill. Not just of mind but of body and spirit too.

When I play a fighting game it is just a hobby. It's escapism. Its' letting my inner child let off some steam so I can better cope with the harshness of the real world. It is something I do but it does not define my value. As such I do not take it seriously!

Just to preface this review, I absolutely suck at fighting games. This game is the reason I got back into Tekken after so many years, and in terms of gameplay, it’s easily the best entry in the series. The combat feels smooth, responsive, and endlessly satisfying thanks to the sheer variety of combos you can pull off. The stages are gorgeous for the most part, and while the soundtrack is decent, it doesn’t stand out as much. The story mode tries to do something ambitious but ultimately falls flat it’s more boring than engaging. The biggest problem, however, is the lack of single player content. If you’re not into multiplayer, there isn’t much here to keep you occupied, which is disappointing. The game also feels unfinished at times, especially considering its rough launch. While the DLCs do flesh things out and improve the experience, there are so many of them that it starts to feel frustrating. That said, this is still one of the most enjoyable modern fighting games and a standout entry in the Tekken franchise. Its diverse character roster and fun new mechanics make it a must-play for anyone who loves competitive fighters.

Overall experience: If you have been playing tekken since the last installments, it's probably a great game to pick up. That said, if you really want to get into fighting games as a beginner, tekken is not the game, UNLESS you are willing to invest hours or maybe even years to learn all the match ups to counter all the cheese most characters dish out (strings, grabs, 50/50s). Instead of focusing on basics, the game kinda allows newbies to just use strings and frame traps to troll each other. And I honestly feel that this game is having an identity crisis (projectile attacks for a few characters, meter for some, etc) It's a lot.  If you are willing to learn, then you would probably get good by the time the next game comes out.  I did enjoy my time playing this game but it is definitely not newbie friendly. ALSO WHY DOES THIS GAME SOMETIMES CRASH? I somewhat regret choosing this as my first fighting game. But I do not regret playing it.

Visuals and Audio: I thought the movements of characters were pretty cool. In my opinion, this could be the best looking fighting game out there as of today. It has a lot to offer in terms of visuals. I enjoyed the music during the fights. There was a pretty good mix of genres for background music.

EDIT: I've played this game for longer hours , learned how to Korean back dash, wavedash , learned some frame data of what is plus and minus, what can trap you, etc.
Tekken ,as a franchise IMO, has the best combat system among all fighting games. And yet I still CANNOT recommend Tekken 7 ( this game) to MOST people. Why?

 Even back then, people have been accused of cheating and with clips posted online now by streamers , there is proof  There is also proof of people who are able to tamper with their profiles and the online system itself  (e.g. a player with a 200 plus win streak). So there is no guarantee that the person you are playing online is of the same rank as you are. I live in Japan. And I play some people online who have hella long win streaks in the SAME rank. How can a person have such a win streak in the same rank if he is indeed playing with people of the same level? I've also searched online about the tendencies of players in certain ranks. And at times, the descriptions online do not match what I play against. It just doesn't seem right to pay your hard earned cash for this lack of security. With all the things goin on now in the world, online is the only way to go but it seems this game wasn't really made for a good online experience. If you can play it offline or within a community though, it is amazing.

On a positive note, I can  recommend this game to people who want to get good before the next Tekken game comes out. Maybe by that time, the devs would fix all the issues that plague Tekken 7. Play Tekken 7 (get it on discount) for the possibility of enjoying the next game to the fullest. [h1] TEKKEN 7 Review[/h1]
[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
[b] TEKKEN 7[/b] is a 3D fighter that keeps players entertained through its core of "practice makes perfect," as there is a lot to learn and master in the depth of this title. The stages and music incorporate beautifully on-screen, adding tension and emotion to every match. Paired with the dynamic relation of fast action with a slow tempo, it creates an environment where fights are agitated, and every round counts. Keep reading to know what makes [b]TEKKEN[/b] 7 excellent!

[h1]The Craft of a Singular Style in a Big Roster[/h1]
[b]TEKKEN 7[/b] features an extensive roster with 49 characters! Each of them shares some common ground in their basic gameplay but has unique styles in handling the combat based on their strengths. [b]Noctis[/b], for example, has a high reach that allows him to defend against attacks or keep opponents at bay. In contrast, other fighters as [b]Eliza[/b], can fill bars to increase the power of their moves and behave more erratically. Playing each character, you would realize that despite some singularities, how you move and face opponents will change drastically.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2118894727

In contrast to the gameplay of its roster, I enjoyed the story less in my time with the game; it is not bad itself, but it was pretty short and lacked more content. Overall it did a stable job in terms of quality. Still, it ends up being more of a "discounted" experience rather than a fully immersive one. I enjoyed that characters speak in their associated language, even though it broke the flow at times since it looks like everyone knows how to talk in about every language. Like when [b]Heihachi[/b] speaks in Japanese and [b]Nina[/b] says in English. 

[h1]An Intricate Dance with Your Opponent [/h1]
The fights in the game are dynamic; they can be fast-paced or have a slow tempo depending on each player's action. It is an intricate dance as [b] TEKKEN[/b] focuses more on figuring out your opponent in 3 rounds. It is about figuring out how your adversary thinks. The more you can predict and adapt on the fly to their play style, the better you will do. Some combos can be extended with walls or [b]Rage Arts[/b] to deal more damage. Also, each character has particular moves, such as projectiles, gap closers, dodging attacks, or movements that cannot be interrupted.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2118895889

Graphically speaking, [b]TEKKEN[/b] leaves something to be desired. Characters' hair can, at times, look bad. At the same time, its visuals fail to impress, feeling more like a title from an older generation. The game carries out as a service with content that is being added to it so. Still, there are titles of the same category looking better. I wish they would have thoroughly worked on this aspect to utilize its stages and character customization.

[h1]Music that Breathes Air and Fire[/h1]
Something I see few people talk about is the fantastic soundtrack that [b]TEKKEN[/b] has. The music is outstanding as it pumps you up, reflecting the energy of combat. Its weight is noticeable as its rhythm changes during the last rounds to exhibit the emotion of the fight. It goes even beyond that as it creates an environment for the players. An example is fan-favorite [b]Infinite Azure[/b], which is harmonic and a track perfect for listening to while in training mode, developing one craft. Meanwhile, [b]Heat Haze[/b] gives the aura of a "final battle" or "betting everything" with the high pumping, melodic singing, and explosiveness of the song!

Customization is another excellent aspect of [b]TEKKEN[/b]! The only thing I noticed that I didn't like is that all items are locked to [b]Treasure Battle.[/b] The mode itself could be better, as it can become pretty stale quickly as you only fight versus the CPU. Getting clothes and accessories to make your characters stand out more becomes tedious grinding. It can serve as some practice in the meantime, and the modifiers are fun at first, but my interest in it died out quickly as it was tedious at best.

[h1] Strong and Weak Points[/h1]
The strong point of this title, in addition to all the gameplay elements, is customization. While, as stated before, the grinding can be tedious, the options at the player's disposal are limitless! From butterfly wings to having a [b]Jenga[/b] on top of your head that keeps crumbling every time you are hit. They can give birth to some incredible characters and glamour and personalize them to your taste. Whenever you want to make your golden warriors, cute fighters, or the most strange ideas, there is a lot to try, and it is a lot of fun!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2118897082

The weak point of [b]TEKKEN[/b] is the barrier for newbies to enter the game. It is easy to get into but hard to master, and the depth of its combat, combos, and characters can be too much for a newer player to wrap their head around. It doesn't help that it has an arcade formula, meaning that there are few flashy moves or assists in helping newbies. There is nothing wrong with any of those elements. It might be daring for newcomers, and lacking tutorials doesn't help. 

[h1]X Notes[/h1]
A fascinating aspect is that rather than making a new entry into the game, [b]Bandai Namco[/b] opted to carry it out as a service and kept adding content. There are guest characters such as [b]Noctis[/b] from [b]Final Fantasy XV,[/b] and [b]Negan[/b] from the [b]Walking Dead[/b] while favorites such as [b]Ganryu[/b] come back! In addition, extra modes and customization options are released as DLC, along with stages. 

Acquiring all of that content can be pretty pricey. For a total of $80, it is quite a high price for all of it. Characters have different prices assigned to them, with guest characters being a bit more expensive. At the same time, modes such a [b]TEKKEN BOWL[/b] can cost the same as up to 3 additional characters while being lacking. They also made the terrible decision of locking frame data behind a paywall, as you have to pay to unlock it when it should have been free. 

The game ran well on a GTX 1060 with an Intel Core i7-8750H resulting in a locked 60FPS with the setting set to max and the render scale of 200%; there are three different season passes.

[h1] Finally…[/h1]
[b] TEKKEN 7[/b] is a fantastic game if you are looking for a fighting game with a lot of depth and are okay with learning and practicing your craft to perfect it. It is more demanding than its peers in the dedication that needs to be put into it. Still, with a lot of content on the base game plus the DLC and the online being solid, it is a good buy for anyone interested in it and for fans of fighting games. I can finally start reviewing this game since I have been playing this fighting game non stop, so let's start the full in depth review

TEKKEN 7 is a long awaited sequel, developed by Bandai Namco Games. Originally, TEKKEN 7 was released on arcades exclusively in South Korea and Japan in 2015. Then the updated version (Fated Retribution) of TEKKEN 7 came out a year later. It has been 6 years since we had a previous TEKKEN game which is Tag Tournament 2. I believe this is the first franchise running on Unreal Engine 4 and it plays smoothly on PC. This is the greatest PC port fighting game I have ever played, period.

[h1]Story:[/h1]
The story starts with Mishima Saga. It starts from the very first game to pretty much at the end. The storytelling is awesome but narrative from the reporter, eh not so much. There are some cliche during Mishima Saga storyline but I accepted it because I have played TEKKEN games previously and the story is always filled with cheesy plot. Speaking of cheesy, the dialogue is just a mess, like what the f*ck. Nina is speaking English towards some soldier who cannot understand English but replied with Japanese dialect anyway and vice versa during main storyline. The final conclusion is somewhat filled with questions that needs to be answered. The final fight though, it's friggin amazing. But first, let me talk about how f*cking amazing the transition is. It went from the cutscene to a gameplay. The story is around 4 to 5 hours when playing on Easy difficulty. Enough of that, there's also another story for all characters called "Character's Episodes". Spoilers, it's unsentimental and somewhat silly.

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]
The gameplay is different compare to traditional 2D fighting games you have played before. It is a 3D fighting game, so there will be a lot of movement required. The combat system plays like a same usual TEKKEN formula. The controls are tight and easy to learn. They implemented Rage Art and Rage Drive. Rage Art is a cinematic special move that can be hit or blocked when guarding at the right time, while Rage Drive is an immediate special move. It can be used only once per round. During Mishima Saga, there is a "Story Assist" where you press the assist button and performs the command you want to perform. This game has some nerve racking moments, where 2 players are clashing against each other and make some amazing plays with cinematic slow motion. There are 39 character rosters so far, but there will be another guest character coming out this year. Bringing Akuma from Street Fighter franchise into this game is a masterpiece. Most of the characters' move list are a f*ckton. I am talking about 80+ command list each character.

[h1]Contents:[/h1]
For this game's content, I have to say, the contents are just bland and shallow. Like this is the first game that made into an eSports oriented game. There are not many casual contents like TEKKEN Bowling (it's coming but it will be a paid DLC), TEKKEN Force and other mode that I cannot remember from the previous games. Arcade mode isn't enough because the playthrough is short and doesn't have endings after beating the final stage. The customisation is around mediocre, but I am going to defend that I like the Player Customisation because you can change the lifebar border, the title and the stats banner thing (I don't know what it is or cannot remember). The soundtrack is cool but it's more of wub wubs and dub dubs. There are some stages' BGM I like but others, not really. They will add cosmetics and contents for Player and Character customisation for free in the future. Unfortunately, the devs decided to release characters from previous TEKKEN games are behind the paywall.

[h1]Multiplayer:[/h1]
Online has 3 modes; Ranked, Player or Casual and Tournament mode. Ranked is more of a "git gud" segment but be aware there will be scrubs that spams punches or same moves. Player Match is a casual mode, where you create a lobby with 8 players and vsing against each other and spectating players if you are not playing and great thing is that you don't need to worry about losing your rank. Tournament mode is an eSports type of game mode, so easy to explain. The netcode of this game, I got to say, it runs smoothly. This has to be a huge improvement of netcode from previous TEKKEN game. Players are debating which platform is better for online play. Well, PC has a faster matchmaking, while PS4 has more playerbase. So it's a personal preference, nothing wrong with console version and PC version.

[h1]Verdict:[/h1]
Man, it has been a while reviewing games. Anyway, is this worth the wait? Well, I'll have to be honest and be real here. For casuals, it's really accessible game, compare to previous games. The content isn't enough to keep the casual players last long but hey bowling game mode is on the way. If you really want to try out the game, wait for the sale, in case of not liking it. DLC characters, it's somewhat divided. For longtime fans, I have to say, this is more of a love/hate relationship. For me personally, I f*cking love it since I have been waiting for a TEKKEN game on PC. The score for this game, it's an 8 out of 10. A solid recommendation for casuals and long awaited fans.
